name: Piram
overview: Piram was a male king who ruled over the city of Jarmuth during the period of Israel's conquest of the land, as recorded in Joshua 10:3. His role as King of Jarmuth places him among the Canaanite leaders opposing Israel's advance. Scripture identifies him specifically by his kingship and city, but does not provide further tribal or familial details.
namesAndTitles: The name 'Piram' possibly means 'wild donkey,' 'indomitable,' or 'zebra,' reflecting characteristics of strength or untamed nature. His title, 'King of Jarmuth,' straightforwardly denotes his royal authority over the city of Jarmuth. Both names are recorded in Joshua 10:3 and are not indicated as being divinely given.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture does not record any family relationships for Piram beyond his identification as King of Jarmuth. There are no known connections to other individuals or tribes mentioned in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Piram's significance lies in his role as one of the Canaanite kings who opposed Israel during the conquest of the Promised Land. As King of Jarmuth, he was part of the coalition of rulers who confronted Joshua and the Israelites, marking him as an adversary in God's unfolding plan to give the land to His people. His mention in Joshua 10:3 situates him within the broader narrative of divine judgment and conquest.
